methodology: Curated policy snapshot. An enacted statute includes narrow testing or pilot laws; EO history includes rescinded orders. Secondary survey classifications require primary-text review. No-policy-record is not a finding that AV operation is legal or illegal. Dates are null when enactment date is unverified.

federal.title: FMVSS barrier review
federal.summary: NHTSA requested public comment on standards that might impede certification or testing of ADS vehicles without human driving controls. This request did not amend a standard.
federal.takeaway: NHTSA requested public comment on standards that might impede certification or testing of ADS vehicles without human driving controls

federal.title: Removing regulatory barriers for ADS vehicles
federal.summary: Advanced notice sought input on adapting crash avoidance standards for vehicles without traditional manual controls; it did not change an FMVSS.
federal.takeaway: Advanced notice sought input on adapting crash avoidance standards for vehicles without traditional manual controls; it did not change an FMVSS

federal.title: Occupant protection proposal
federal.summary: Proposed adapting 11 numbered crash protection standards for ADS vehicles without conventional driving controls; the final rule later added changes to 212 and 219.
federal.takeaway: Proposed adapting 11 numbered crash protection standards for ADS vehicles without conventional driving controls; the final rule later added changes to 212 and 219

federal.title: Occupant protection final rule
federal.summary: Amended 13 numbered standards for ADS vehicles without traditional manual driving controls, including FMVSS 204's exclusion for vehicles without steering controls. This addresses vehicle crash protection, not ADS driving performance.
federal.takeaway: Amended 13 numbered standards for ADS vehicles without traditional manual driving controls, including FMVSS 204's exclusion for vehicles without steering controls

federal.title: Steering control rearward displacement · FMVSS 204
federal.summary: A separate, generally applicable rule excludes vehicles certified to FMVSS 208 frontal barrier crash protection from FMVSS 204's steering column rearward displacement requirements and removes obsolete text. It is relevant to AV design but is not an ADS-specific rule.
federal.takeaway: Exempts FMVSS 208-certified vehicles from the steering-column displacement test

federal.title: Transmission displays · FMVSS 102
federal.summary: Proposed changes to requirements written around human-operated transmission controls in ADS-equipped vehicles.
federal.takeaway: Would adapt transmission-display rules for vehicles without manual controls

federal.title: Defrosting and windshield wiping · FMVSS 103/104
federal.summary: Proposed changes to defrosting and wiping requirements for ADS vehicles without conventional driver controls.
federal.takeaway: Would adapt defrosting and wiper rules for driverless designs

federal.title: Tire placards · FMVSS 110
federal.summary: Proposed adapting tire information placard requirements to ADS-equipped vehicle designs.
federal.takeaway: Would adapt tire-information placards for ADS vehicle designs

federal.title: Brake controls · FMVSS 135
federal.summary: Proposed removing the manual brake pedal requirement for vehicles designed exclusively for ADS operation while retaining braking performance requirements.
federal.takeaway: Would remove the brake-pedal requirement for ADS-only vehicles; braking standards remain

federal.title: FMVSS 201 · Interior impact
federal.summary: Revised interior impact applicability and test references for vehicles without a conventional driver's seating position.
federal.takeaway: Adapts interior-impact tests for vehicles without a driver seat

federal.title: FMVSS 203 · Steering control impact
federal.summary: Excluded vehicles without steering controls from the steering control impact standard.
federal.takeaway: Exempts vehicles without steering controls from steering-control impact tests

federal.title: FMVSS 204 · Steering control rearward displacement
federal.summary: Excluded vehicles without steering controls from the steering column displacement standard.
federal.takeaway: Exempts vehicles without steering controls from steering-column displacement tests

federal.title: FMVSS 205 · Glazing materials
federal.summary: Updated the glazing standard's application to trucks designed to carry at least one person.
federal.takeaway: Updates glazing rules for trucks designed to carry occupants

federal.title: FMVSS 206 · Door locks and retention
federal.summary: Updated door definitions and applicability for vehicles without a conventional driver's seating position.
federal.takeaway: Updates door-lock rules for vehicles without a conventional driver seat

federal.title: FMVSS 207 · Seating systems
federal.summary: Required a designated driver's seat only where manually operated driving controls are present.
federal.takeaway: Requires a driver seat only when manual driving controls are present

federal.title: FMVSS 208 · Occupant crash protection
federal.summary: Revised crash protection requirements, seating terminology and test procedures for vehicles without manual driving controls.
federal.takeaway: Adapts occupant crash protection and testing for vehicles without manual controls

federal.title: FMVSS 212 · Windshield mounting
federal.summary: Conforming applicability change for trucks designed to carry at least one person, added in the final rule.
federal.takeaway: Updates windshield-mounting coverage for trucks carrying occupants

federal.title: FMVSS 214 · Side impact protection
federal.summary: Revised side impact test procedures and seating references for vehicles without traditional driver controls.
federal.takeaway: Adapts side-impact tests for vehicles without conventional driver controls

federal.title: FMVSS 216a · Roof crush resistance
federal.summary: Updated applicability and test setup for roof crush protection in vehicles designed to carry occupants.
federal.takeaway: Updates roof-crush test setup for vehicles designed to carry occupants

federal.title: FMVSS 219 · Windshield zone intrusion
federal.summary: Conforming applicability change for trucks designed to carry at least one person, added in the final rule.
federal.takeaway: Updates windshield-intrusion coverage for trucks carrying occupants

federal.title: FMVSS 225 · Child restraint anchorages
federal.summary: Revised the shuttle bus definition to account for buses without manual driving controls.
federal.takeaway: Updates the shuttle-bus definition for buses without manual controls

federal.title: FMVSS 226 · Ejection mitigation
federal.summary: Updated applicability and test setup for ejection mitigation in vehicles without conventional driver controls.
federal.takeaway: Adapts ejection-mitigation tests for vehicles without conventional driver controls

federal_oversight.title: Standing General Order crash reporting
federal_oversight.summary: NHTSA ordered specified ADS and Level 2 ADAS crash reports from manufacturers and operators; the reports are not determinations of fault.
federal_oversight.takeaway: NHTSA ordered specified ADS and Level 2 ADAS crash reports from manufacturers and operators; the reports are not determinations of fault

federal_oversight.title: Third amended Standing General Order
federal_oversight.summary: NHTSA revised ADS crash reporting requirements in April 2025. Review the current order and amendments for applicable thresholds and deadlines.
federal_oversight.takeaway: NHTSA revised ADS crash reporting requirements in April 2025

federal_oversight.title: AV STEP proposal
federal_oversight.summary: Proposed a voluntary ADS safety transparency and evaluation program. NHTSA withdrew this proposal in June 2026; no AV STEP program took effect.
federal_oversight.takeaway: Proposed a voluntary ADS safety transparency and evaluation program

federal_oversight.title: AV STEP withdrawal
federal_oversight.summary: NHTSA formally withdrew the 2025 AV STEP proposed rulemaking.
federal_oversight.takeaway: NHTSA formally withdrew the 2025 AV STEP proposed rulemaking

states.name: Alabama
states.analysis: Alabama's AV-specific statute governs automated commercial vehicles. Its scope does not establish a general passenger robotaxi pathway.
states.oversight: Alabama DOT has state-level jurisdiction under the commercial vehicle framework.

states.name: Alaska
states.framework: No enacted AV operation framework identified
states.analysis: Proposals to restrict autonomous operation and assign operator liability remained under consideration in the 2026 survey. Proposed bills are not current operating authority.
states.oversight: General motor vehicle law applies while the proposed AV measures remain unenacted.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Arizona
states.analysis: Arizona's AV framework grew from executive orders in 2015 and 2018. The state provides notification and certification guidance before testing and operation. A company operating in Arizona should not be interpreted as having statewide service coverage.
states.oversight: Arizona MVD notification and certification.
states.source_label: Arizona DOT AV framework and HB 2813 history

states.name: Arkansas
states.analysis: Arkansas permits driverless operation when statutory conditions and advance submissions, including commercial-purpose information, are satisfied.
states.oversight: State submission and applicable traffic and vehicle rules.

states.name: California
states.analysis: DMV regulates AV testing and deployment under Articles 3.7 and 3.8. Its 2026 update followed a draft, formal proposal and two modified comment rounds. CPUC separately authorizes passenger service: test pilots cannot charge fares, while deployment programs can. A DMV permit alone does not authorize paid rides.
states.oversight: DMV: vehicle testing, deployment permits and reporting. CPUC: passenger service pilots, fare-charging deployment, passenger safety and service reporting.

states.name: Colorado
states.framework: AV operating framework; truck restrictions vetoed
states.analysis: Colorado has an AV statute, while proposed in-vehicle human requirements for automated commercial trucks were vetoed in both 2025 and 2026. A vetoed bill cannot be treated as a current restriction.
states.oversight: State motor vehicle law and any applicable testing conditions.

states.name: Connecticut
states.analysis: Connecticut's dedicated AV pathway centers on a limited pilot involving selected municipalities. A pilot law is not blanket authority for commercial deployment statewide.
states.oversight: Pilot approval and participating municipalities.

states.name: Delaware
states.framework: No enacted AV-specific operating statute identified
states.analysis: Delaware's 2025 proposal to require an onboard operator failed. Its AV advisory activity does not itself grant a commercial permit.
states.oversight: Ordinary vehicle rules; no distinct statewide commercial AV permit identified in the guide.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Florida
states.analysis: Florida law allows driverless AV operation subject to statutory conditions. This review has not established a separate public company-level permit roster; a service announcement is not a state-issued ODD boundary.
states.oversight: Vehicle registration and statutory operating requirements.

states.name: Georgia
states.analysis: Georgia enacted rules for fully autonomous vehicles through SB 219. The Observatory has operating evidence, but has not located a public state holder roster; the statute and an operator's actual service geography answer different questions.
states.oversight: State motor vehicle law and applicable service regulation.

states.name: Hawaii
states.analysis: Act 21 (2020) established a state AV testing pilot with an onboard human driver and a report to the 2023 legislature. It did not grant broad driverless commercial authority.
states.oversight: Hawaii DOT determined eligible pilot testers.

states.name: Idaho
states.analysis: Idaho's executive-order committee examined testing and deployment issues. The 2026 survey identified no enacted AV-specific operating statute.
states.oversight: General motor vehicle requirements and agency guidance.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Illinois
states.analysis: Illinois law limits local governments' ability to prohibit AVs, but that rule alone does not establish a statewide permit or demonstrate an active commercial service.
states.oversight: State vehicle and traffic law; local powers are constrained by statute.

states.name: Indiana
states.framework: No enacted AV-specific operating statute identified
states.analysis: Indiana's 2025 bill addressing autonomous tractor-trailers failed. The 2026 survey did not identify a dedicated AV operating law.
states.oversight: Ordinary vehicle and commercial-carrier requirements.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Iowa
states.analysis: Iowa's statute addresses operation of automated driving systems. Multiple proposed 2026 changes failed, so those proposals should not be counted as current conditions.
states.oversight: State traffic and vehicle requirements under Iowa's AV statute.

states.name: Kansas
states.analysis: Kansas law accommodates private and commercial AV operation subject to statutory conditions. This permission says nothing about a particular company's ODD.
states.oversight: State vehicle and traffic rules.

states.name: Kentucky
states.analysis: Kentucky's AV framework took effect in 2024. The survey reports that a temporary onboard-driver rule for very heavy commercial vehicles expired in August 2026 after an extension failed.
states.oversight: State vehicle law and any remaining commercial-carrier requirements.

states.name: Louisiana
states.analysis: Louisiana's dedicated AV operating provisions focus on commercial uses. Passenger service cannot be inferred from that freight-oriented authority.
states.oversight: State commercial-vehicle and traffic requirements.

states.name: Maine
states.analysis: Maine authorizes transportation officials to establish AV pilot activity. The guide does not describe a broad commercial robotaxi approval regime.
states.oversight: Maine DOT pilot rules and general vehicle requirements.

states.name: Maryland
states.analysis: Maryland's AV-specific statute focuses on converted vehicles for commercial or industrial use. Broader 2025 operation and safety-operator bills did not pass.
states.oversight: Motor Vehicle Administration and applicable vehicle law.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.analysis: Executive Order 572 established a testing framework in 2016 and was rescinded by Executive Order 603 in 2022. Current testing authority needs separate verification.
states.oversight: Do not rely on the rescinded order for current testing.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Michigan
states.analysis: Michigan law covers research, testing and operation and permits driverless use under statutory conditions, including minimal-risk capability and insurance. SAVE projects have separate manufacturer limits.
states.oversight: State AV statutes and vehicle rules.

states.name: Minnesota
states.framework: No comprehensive AV operation law enacted
states.analysis: Minnesota proposed an AV and on-demand network framework in 2026, but it failed. The proposal should not be represented as an active permit system.
states.oversight: General vehicle rules and any relevant agency guidance.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Mississippi
states.analysis: Mississippi allows a person to operate an AV when statutory conditions are met. The permission is broader than a manufacturer-only test program.
states.oversight: State traffic, registration, and safety requirements.

states.name: Missouri
states.analysis: A Missouri proposal requiring an active human driver was still pending in the survey. Its introduction alone does not change current AV operating law.
states.oversight: General state motor vehicle and carrier rules.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Montana
states.analysis: Montana enacted measures addressing automated vehicles and platooning in 2025. The exact authority for a proposed passenger or freight service requires examination of the relevant provisions.
states.oversight: State vehicle and commercial-carrier requirements.

states.name: Nebraska
states.analysis: Nebraska permits ADS-equipped vehicles with an onboard licensed driver and provides a conditional pathway for operation without one.
states.oversight: State statutory requirements for driverless operation and ordinary vehicle law.

states.name: Nevada
states.analysis: Nevada provides separate DMV applications for autonomous-vehicle testing and certification for operation. No complete public list of current holders was found in the sources reviewed.
states.oversight: Nevada DMV testing and operation certification.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.analysis: New Hampshire provides a testing pilot and an AV advisory commission. Those provisions do not establish general commercial deployment statewide.
states.oversight: Pilot approval and commission reporting.

states.name: New Jersey
states.analysis: A 2026 bill proposed a fully autonomous vehicle pilot. The guide identifies it as pending, so a proposed pilot cannot be shown as active authorization.
states.oversight: General motor vehicle rules pending enacted AV legislation.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: New Mexico
states.analysis: New Mexico's AV framework addresses testing and requires advance notification. A testing notice is distinct from commercial deployment approval.
states.oversight: State transportation and testing-notification requirements.

states.name: New York
states.framework: State demonstration permit; additional NYC test permit
states.analysis: Testing in New York City requires a New York State DMV demonstration or testing permit and a separate NYC DOT permit. A NYC testing permit does not authorize commercial passenger service.
states.oversight: NYS DMV demonstration program; NYC DOT testing permit within the city.
states.source_label: New York State DMV AV demonstration

states.name: North Carolina
states.analysis: North Carolina has AV-specific operating provisions and a committee charged with recommendations for testing and deployment. A statewide law does not reveal a company's actual service area.
states.oversight: State traffic law and committee-led policy review.

states.name: North Dakota
states.analysis: North Dakota permits autonomous operation subject to applicable state and federal law. A 2025 AV funding proposal failed.
states.oversight: Ordinary vehicle law plus the state's AV operating provision.

states.name: Ohio
states.analysis: Ohio's DriveOhio program requires companies to register before AV testing. The guide identifies no general AV operation statute; registration should not be read as commercial deployment approval.
states.oversight: DriveOhio testing registration and state vehicle rules.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Oklahoma
states.analysis: Oklahoma permits AV operation when statutory conditions and ordinary registration rules are satisfied; on-demand networks also remain subject to applicable service law.
states.oversight: State traffic, registration, and on-demand network requirements.

states.name: Oregon
states.framework: Task force, no general operating law
states.analysis: Oregon established an AV task force. A 2026 proposal to permit operation without ordinary driving privileges failed.
states.oversight: General vehicle law while broader AV operation proposals remain unenacted.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.analysis: Pennsylvania's AV pathway places oversight with PennDOT and requires self-certification. A separate 2025 certificate proposal was pending in the survey.
states.oversight: PennDOT self-certification and state traffic requirements.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.framework: No dedicated AV operating law identified
states.analysis: The 2026 survey identifies no AV-specific statute or new proposal. That does not establish that an individual deployment is authorized.
states.oversight: General motor vehicle and service rules.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: South Carolina
states.framework: No dedicated AV operating law identified
states.analysis: South Carolina's survey entry identifies no new AV legislation since 2018. Operator status still depends on general vehicle law and any service-specific rules.
states.oversight: General state motor vehicle requirements.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: South Dakota
states.analysis: South Dakota added an AV operating statute in 2024 alongside earlier platooning provisions. Commercial freight and passenger services should be assessed under their relevant requirements.
states.oversight: State AV, commercial-carrier, and traffic rules.

states.name: Tennessee
states.analysis: Tennessee has a general AV operating framework. A 2026 amendment addresses traffic violations committed by AVs, adding a distinct accountability issue to the state's policy picture.
states.oversight: State traffic law and the Automated Vehicles Act.

states.name: Texas
states.analysis: Texas authorized AV operation in 2017 and added a mandatory TxDMV authorization for commercial automated-vehicle operation in 2026. The state does not publish a complete public holder roster in the sources reviewed; documented service is distinct from authorization.
states.oversight: TxDMV commercial authorization; traffic-law and insurance requirements.

states.name: Utah
states.analysis: Utah's AV law governs operation of ADS-equipped vehicles subject to state and federal requirements. A 2026 information-request bill failed.
states.oversight: State AV statute and ordinary traffic requirements.

states.name: Vermont
states.analysis: Vermont's AV law addresses testing only, with public comment and an onboard human driver for each approved test. It is not a general driverless passenger-service pathway.
states.oversight: Test-specific approval and public-comment process.

states.name: Virginia
states.analysis: Virginia considered autonomous operation licenses in SB 670, but the measure was continued to 2027 in the survey. Its proposed licenses are not existing permits.
states.oversight: General vehicle law pending any enacted AV-specific licensing framework.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Washington
states.analysis: Washington distinguishes eligibility to test AVs on public roads from registration of the vehicle itself. Neither alone identifies an operating service area.
states.oversight: State testing self-certification and vehicle registration processes.

states.name: West Virginia
states.analysis: West Virginia's AV law accommodates several service types subject to conditions. Driverless operators must submit a law-enforcement interaction plan before operating.
states.oversight: State vehicle rules and law-enforcement interaction plan.
states.source_label: West Virginia Fully Autonomous Vehicle Act

states.name: Wisconsin
states.analysis: Wisconsin's AV steering committee addressed testing and deployment policy. Proposed 2026 board and permit legislation failed, leaving no such new permit in force.
states.oversight: General vehicle rules and existing agency coordination.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: Wyoming
states.analysis: The 2026 guide identifies no AV-specific operating law or new proposal in Wyoming. That finding does not amount to a positive authorization for any proposed service.
states.oversight: General motor vehicle and commercial-carrier rules.
states.source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

states.name: District of Columbia
states.analysis: District rules address AV testing with a human behind the wheel; a testing provision is not commercial deployment authorization.
states.oversight: DDOT oversight.
states.source_label: DDOT AV law and testing guidance

state_events.summary: South Dakota added an AV operating statute in 2024 alongside earlier platooning provisions. Commercial freight and passenger services should be assessed under their relevant requirements.
state_events.takeaway: South Dakota added an AV operating statute in 2024 alongside earlier platooning provisions

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: Tennessee has a general AV operating framework. A 2026 amendment addresses traffic violations committed by AVs, adding a distinct accountability issue to the state's policy picture.
state_events.takeaway: Tennessee has a general AV operating framework

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: Texas authorized AV operation in 2017 and added a mandatory TxDMV authorization for commercial automated-vehicle operation in 2026. The state does not publish a complete public holder roster in the sources reviewed; documented service is distinct from authorization.
state_events.takeaway: Texas authorized AV operation in 2017 and added a mandatory TxDMV authorization for commercial automated-vehicle operation in 2026

state_events.title: SB 2807 · commercial AV authorization
state_events.summary: Added a TxDMV authorization program for commercial AV operation; the authorization requirement became enforceable May 28, 2026.
state_events.takeaway: Added a TxDMV authorization program for commercial AV operation; the authorization requirement became enforceable May 28, 2026

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: Utah's AV law governs operation of ADS-equipped vehicles subject to state and federal requirements. A 2026 information-request bill failed.
state_events.takeaway: Utah's AV law governs operation of ADS-equipped vehicles subject to state and federal requirements

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: Vermont's AV law addresses testing only, with public comment and an onboard human driver for each approved test. It is not a general driverless passenger-service pathway.
state_events.takeaway: Vermont's AV law addresses testing only, with public comment and an onboard human driver for each approved test

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: Washington distinguishes eligibility to test AVs on public roads from registration of the vehicle itself. Neither alone identifies an operating service area.
state_events.takeaway: Washington distinguishes eligibility to test AVs on public roads from registration of the vehicle itself

state_events.title: Washington Executive Order 17-02
state_events.summary: Created a state testing coordination and self-certification framework.
state_events.takeaway: Created a state testing coordination and self-certification framework

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: West Virginia's AV law accommodates several service types subject to conditions. Driverless operators must submit a law-enforcement interaction plan before operating.
state_events.takeaway: West Virginia's AV law accommodates several service types subject to conditions
state_events.source_label: West Virginia Fully Autonomous Vehicle Act

state_events.title: Wisconsin Executive Order 245
state_events.summary: Created a steering committee on AV testing and deployment; the order specified dissolution after a 2018 final report.
state_events.takeaway: Created a steering committee on AV testing and deployment; the order specified dissolution after a 2018 final report

state_events.title: Enacted AV statute · current framework
state_events.summary: District rules address AV testing with a human behind the wheel; a testing provision is not commercial deployment authorization.
state_events.takeaway: District rules address AV testing with a human behind the wheel; a testing provision is not commercial deployment authorization
state_events.source_label: DDOT AV law and testing guidance

state_events.title: SB 1298 · AV testing framework
state_events.summary: Directed California DMV to establish testing regulations and created a statutory framework for autonomous vehicles; later statutes and regulations changed the program.
state_events.takeaway: Directed California DMV to establish testing regulations and created a statutory framework for autonomous vehicles; later statutes and regulations changed the program

state_events.title: AB 511 · first AV framework
state_events.summary: Required Nevada DMV regulations authorizing autonomous vehicle operation and established early testing and licensing provisions; later amendments expanded the framework.
state_events.takeaway: Required Nevada DMV regulations authorizing autonomous vehicle operation and established early testing and licensing provisions; later amendments expanded the framework

state_events.title: AB 69 · driverless transportation services
state_events.summary: Revised testing and operation provisions and provided for fully autonomous transportation services and network companies under state oversight.
state_events.takeaway: Revised testing and operation provisions and provided for fully autonomous transportation services and network companies under state oversight

state_events.title: HB 7027 · AV operating changes
state_events.summary: Revised Florida's autonomous vehicle operating and equipment rules; this preceded the broader 2019 driverless operation law.
state_events.takeaway: Revised Florida's autonomous vehicle operating and equipment rules; this preceded the broader 2019 driverless operation law

state_events.title: HB 311 · driverless operation
state_events.summary: Authorized a fully autonomous vehicle to operate without a human operator and addressed on-demand AV networks and insurance.
state_events.takeaway: Authorized a fully autonomous vehicle to operate without a human operator and addressed on-demand AV networks and insurance

state_events.title: DMV · driverless testing and deployment proposal
state_events.summary: DMV proposed a regulatory framework for driverless testing and deployment, followed by modified texts in October and November 2017.
state_events.takeaway: DMV proposed a regulatory framework for driverless testing and deployment, followed by modified texts in October and November 2017

state_events.title: DMV · light-duty delivery vehicle rules
state_events.summary: DMV began accepting applications under approved rules for autonomous delivery trucks below 10,001 pounds. Operation still required a DMV permit.
state_events.takeaway: DMV began accepting applications under approved rules for autonomous delivery trucks below 10,001 pounds

state_events.title: DMV · draft testing and deployment update
state_events.summary: DMV requested public comments on draft changes to Articles 3.7 (testing) and 3.8 (deployment). This was an early draft, not adopted text.
state_events.takeaway: DMV requested public comments on draft changes to Articles 3.7 (testing) and 3.8 (deployment)

state_events.title: DMV · formal regulatory proposal
state_events.summary: DMV published proposed changes to Articles 3.7 and 3.8 and its initial statement of reasons; the initial comment period ended June 9, 2025.
state_events.takeaway: DMV published proposed changes to Articles 3.7 and 3.8 and its initial statement of reasons; the initial comment period ended June 9, 2025

state_events.title: DMV · first modified proposal
state_events.summary: DMV released revised regulatory text for another comment round, which closed December 18, 2025.
state_events.takeaway: DMV released revised regulatory text for another comment round, which closed December 18, 2025

state_events.title: DMV · second modified proposal
state_events.summary: DMV released a second revision of Articles 3.7 and 3.8; comments closed February 5, 2026.
state_events.takeaway: DMV released a second revision of Articles 3.7 and 3.8; comments closed February 5, 2026

state_events.title: DMV · updated testing and deployment rules effective
state_events.summary: The adopted Article 3.7 testing and Article 3.8 deployment updates took effect. Testing data reporting has a 120-day implementation period; deployment reports begin after the first full calendar quarter following the effective date.
state_events.takeaway: The adopted Article 3.7 testing and Article 3.8 deployment updates took effect

state_events.title: CPUC · passenger service pilots
state_events.summary: Decision 18-05-043 authorized drivered and driverless test AV passenger service. These pilots require a corresponding DMV testing permit and cannot charge fares.
state_events.takeaway: Decision 18-05-043 authorized drivered and driverless test AV passenger service

state_events.title: CPUC · paid passenger deployment framework
state_events.summary: Decision 20-11-046, as modified by 21-05-017, authorized drivered and driverless paid passenger service programs. Deployment applicants also need a DMV deployment permit; driverless applicants submit a Passenger Safety Plan.
state_events.takeaway: Decision 20-11-046, as modified by 21-05-017, authorized drivered and driverless paid passenger service programs

state_events.title: CPUC · enhanced passenger service reporting
state_events.summary: CPUC adopted enhanced AV reporting after a 2023 workshop and public comments, extending oversight of passenger safety and service activity.
state_events.takeaway: CPUC adopted enhanced AV reporting after a 2023 workshop and public comments, extending oversight of passenger safety and service activity

city_events.title: NYC DOT AV testing permit
city_events.summary: The city requires its own testing permit on top of the New York State DMV demonstration permit, with a trained human test operator in the driver's seat. This is a testing program, not commercial deployment approval.
city_events.takeaway: The city requires its own testing permit on top of the New York State DMV demonstration permit, with a trained human test operator in the driver's seat

city_events.title: Seattle AV testing permit
city_events.summary: SDOT established a Street Use permit for AV tests, including an onboard test driver and first responder plan. First permits were issued in 2023.
city_events.takeaway: SDOT established a Street Use permit for AV tests, including an onboard test driver and first responder plan

city_events.title: State-led passenger service oversight
city_events.summary: California DMV permits underlying AV operation and CPUC permits passenger service. SFMTA manages city streets and curb policy and participates in state proceedings; it does not issue the statewide AV passenger permit.
city_events.takeaway: California DMV permits underlying AV operation and CPUC permits passenger service

city_events.title: Market Street pickup and drop-off access
city_events.summary: The city began allowing Waymo passenger pickup and drop-off on Market Street under local street-use rules.
city_events.takeaway: The city began allowing Waymo passenger pickup and drop-off on Market Street under local street-use rules

city_events.title: AV coordination under Texas preemption
city_events.summary: Texas places AV operation oversight with the state. Austin publishes public-safety and street coordination information but does not grant a separate AV operating authorization.
city_events.takeaway: Texas places AV operation oversight with the state

city_events.title: Boston AV testing approach
city_events.summary: Boston's earlier testing approach used a local memorandum of understanding. The city's published program information includes historical approvals and should not be read as a current permit roster.
city_events.takeaway: Boston's earlier testing approach used a local memorandum of understanding
